mainTopic: Pregnancy length, how long before birth labor pains (קושי) make bleeding pure, and the dispute over labor bleeding during the days of purity
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: the חסידים הראשונים timed marital relations so that a birth would not lead to חילול שבת, and the גמרא reads it as 'from Wednesday onward.' מר זוטרא then learns the 271-day minimum pregnancy from the גימטריא of הריון. He also shows from the birth of שמואל הנביא that a seven-month baby can be born after incomplete months. Next, שמואל explains from 'וטמאה שבועים כנדתה' why רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say labor pains (קושי) count for only two weeks before birth. A ברייתא then works out that a woman can bleed for up to 25 days before birth without becoming a זבה, but not for 26. רבא explains that the purity of labor pains does not apply to a נפל. A new משנה then brings a dispute about labor bleeding during the 80 days after a girl's birth. The חכמים use a קל וחומר to call it pure, and רבי אליעזר answers with the rule of דיו that it still makes her a נדה. רבא adds a reading of ״מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ״ that supports רבי אליעזר, and ״תֵּשֵׁב״ teaches that the whole period follows one rule. The amud ends with the start of a new משנה: during the eleven days of זיבה, a woman is presumed pure.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: avoiding חילול שבת
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the ברייתא about the חסידים הראשונים: they timed relations so their wives would not come to חילול שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...so that their wives would not come to desecrate שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא that started on the previous page. The חסידים הראשונים had relations only on Wednesday so that a birth would not lead to חילול שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא follows שמואל's view that a full pregnancy lasts 271, 272 or 273 days. Relations on Sunday, Monday or Tuesday could lead to a birth on שבת. Wednesday avoids that.

keyTerms.meaning: Desecrating שבת, for example by doing work needed for a woman giving birth
The early generations of especially pious people

phrases.english: to a desecration of Shabbat.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: the חסידים had relations only on Wednesday so their wives would not come to this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִידֵי חִלּוּל שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חסידים הראשונים timed relations so that birth would not fall on שבת.

steps.title: Why only Wednesday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says only Wednesday, when later days would also avoid a שבת birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only on Wednesday and no other day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. Thursday, Friday or שבת would also prevent a birth on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the ברייתא's own reasoning, only relations on Sunday, Monday or Tuesday could lead to a birth on שבת. Thursday, Friday or שבת would also avoid that, so limiting the practice to Wednesday alone makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more? Only this and no other?
The fourth day of the week, Wednesday

phrases.english: On a Wednesday, and nothing more?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּרְבִיעִי וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just finished
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that they had relations only on Wednesday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thursday through שבת also avoid a שבת birth, so 'only Wednesday' seems too narrow.

steps.title: Read it as 'from Wednesday onward'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means from Wednesday onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: from Wednesday and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא differently. It means any day from Wednesday on, not only Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the practice matches the reasoning. They avoided only Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, the days that could lead to a שבת birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way instead)
And onward

phrases.english: Say: from Wednesday onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: מֵרְבִיעִי וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allowed only Wednesday itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: It allowed Wednesday and the days after it, and avoided only Sunday to Tuesday.
steps.whatToRemember: The חסידים הראשונים avoided relations early in the week so that a full-term birth (271 to 273 days) would not fall on שבת.

steps.title: The source for 271 days: the word הריון
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא learns the 271-day minimum from the גימטריא of הריון in the פסוק about רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: What is the reason of the חסידים הראשונים? The פסוק says, 'and ה׳ gave her conception (הריון).' The letters of הריון add up to 271.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a source from a פסוק for the חסידים הראשונים' view. A full pregnancy lasts at least 271 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of הריון are ה (5), ר (200), י (10), ו (6) and ן (50), which total 271. So the word for pregnancy itself hints at how long it lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?
The number value of a word's letters
Pregnancy, conception

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
What is the reasoning of the early pious men?
As it is written: "And the Lord gave her conception"
phrases.notes: רות 4:13, about רות and בועז. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: "Herayon" in numerical value
is two hundred and seventy-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דַּחֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the 271-day idea behind the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum length of a full pregnancy, 271 days, is hinted at in the גימטריא of הריון.

steps.title: A seven-month baby can be born after incomplete months
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא teaches that even those who require nine full months for a nine-month birth agree that a seven-month birth can come after incomplete months. He proves it from חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Even the one who holds that a nine-month birth never comes after incomplete months agrees that a seven-month birth can. The פסוק says, 'And it was at the turn of the seasons of the days that חנה conceived and bore a son.' The smallest number of 'seasons' is two, and the smallest number of 'days' is two.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds a second rule. A baby born in the seventh month does not need seven full months. He proves it from the birth of שמואל הנביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seasons' in the plural means at least two, which is six months, since each season is three months. 'Days' in the plural means at least two days. So שמואל was born after six months and two days, early in the seventh month.

keyTerms.meaning: Incomplete (months): born partway through a month
Seasons of the year, three months each
The smallest number a plural word can mean, which is two

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. For a nine-month birth this view still requires full months. Only a seven-month birth can come after incomplete months.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra says:
Even according to the one who said
one who gives birth at nine months does not give birth after incomplete months,
one who gives birth at seven months can give birth after incomplete months,
as it is stated: "And it came to pass, at the seasons of the days,
that Hannah conceived and bore a son",
the minimum of "seasons" is two,
the minimum of "days" is two.
phrases.notes: So the total is six months and two days, which puts the birth in the seventh month.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יוֹלֶדֶת לְתִשְׁעָה אֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת לִמְקוּטָּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by מר זוטרא on pregnancy length, limiting the full-months rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seven-month birth can come after incomplete months, even for those who require full months for a nine-month birth.
steps.whatToRemember: Nine-month births need full months, at least 271 days. Seven-month births can come after incomplete months, as with שמואל, who was born after six months and two days.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: labor pains last at most two weeks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's view of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון that קושי lasts no more than two weeks before birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: labor pains do not last more than two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון. This sets up the next step, where שמואל gives their reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks how long before birth bleeding with labor pains counts as birth-related, so that the woman does not become a זבה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון give the shortest window: two weeks.

keyTerms.meaning: Labor pains, difficulty before giving birth
Here it means weeks

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
There are no labor pains more than two weeks before birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: אֵין קוֹשִׁי יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from pregnancy length back to a new clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Labor pains that make the blood pure last at most two weeks before birth.

steps.title: שמואל's source: 'two weeks as in her נידה'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל derives the two-week limit from the פסוק 'וטמאה שבועים כנדתה'. She is like a נידה but not like a זבה, so her pre-birth bleeding is pure for two weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: What is the reason of these רבנן? The פסוק says, 'And she shall be impure for two weeks, as in her נידה.' Like her נידה and not like her זיבה, which shows that her זיבה is pure. And for how long? Two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains where רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון learn their two weeks. He reads a hint into the פסוק about a woman who gives birth to a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כנדתה,' like her נידה, and not like her זיבה. So bleeding connected to the birth does not make her a זבה. The 'two weeks' in the same פסוק tells us how long before birth this applies.

keyTerms.meaning: As in her menstrual impurity
Her זיבה, bleeding outside her normal time that can make her a זבה
By inference, from this we learn
Two weeks

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule that bleeding with labor pains during the two weeks before birth does not make a woman a זבה, according to רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
What is the reasoning of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: 'The Rabbis' here means רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון from the previous step.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And she shall be impure two weeks, as in her menstruation"
as in her menstruation, and not as in her ziva,
by inference, her ziva is pure.
And for how long? Two weeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה view quoted in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bleeding connected to the birth is not זיבה, and this applies for two weeks, learned from 'שבועים כנדתה'.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: labor pains count for up to two weeks before birth. Source: 'וטמאה שבועים כנדתה', which means like נידה and not like זיבה.

steps.title: A woman can have labor pains for twenty-five days without becoming a זבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows how 25 days of bleeding before birth can be arranged so that she never becomes a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A woman can bleed with labor pains for twenty-five days and still not become a זבה. How? Two days at the end of her זיבה days, then seven days of נידה, then the first two days of זיבה after the נידה, and then fourteen days in which the coming child makes her bleeding pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that builds on שמואל's two-week rule. It shows the longest stretch of bleeding before birth that still does not make her a זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After her seven days of נידה come eleven days of זיבה, and three bleeding days in a row during those days make her a זבה. Here she only has two bleeding days at the end of the eleven, then the seven נידה days, then two at the start of the next eleven. The last fourteen days are pure because of the two-week rule of labor pains, so she never reaches three days in a row.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman having labor pains (קושי) before giving birth
The status of a זבה, which comes from bleeding three days in a row during the days that are not her נידה days
Not at her normal time, meaning during her זיבה days and not during her נידה days
The seven days of her normal monthly period
The coming child makes the bleeding pure, from the two-week rule of labor pains

steps.confusionAlert: The twenty-five days are not counted from the start of her cycle. They begin with the LAST two of her eleven זיבה days, so that those two days are cut off by the נידה days that follow.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There is a woman who has labor pains for twenty-five days,
and the status of a זבה does not come about in them.
How so?
Two days not at her time,
phrases.notes: These are the last two of her eleven זיבה days, the tenth and eleventh.

phrases.english: and seven days of נידה,
and two days after the נידה days,
and fourteen days in which the child makes her pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יֵשׁ מְקַשָּׁה עֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's two-week limit to work out the longest possible stretch of bleeding before birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Up to twenty-five days of bleeding with labor pains can be arranged so that she never becomes a זבה.

steps.title: Twenty-six days of labor pains always make her a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: with twenty-six days it is impossible for her to avoid becoming a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is impossible for a woman to have labor pains for twenty-six days without a child and not give birth as a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side of the limit: one more day, twenty-six, and she must be a זבה when she gives birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With twenty-six days there is no way to arrange them so you avoid three bleeding זיבה days in a row. Whatever extra day you add creates a third day in a row that the two-week purity does not cover. The puzzling words 'without a child' will be discussed in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible
A woman who gives birth while she is a זבה, which brings stricter rules after the birth

phrases.english: And it is impossible for her to have labor pains
for twenty-six days without a child,
and not be a woman who gives birth as a זבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתִּתְקַשֶּׁה עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the upper limit, one day past step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twenty-six days of bleeding with labor pains will always make her a זבה when she gives birth.

steps.title: Without a child, three days should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if there is no child at all, she becomes a זבה after three days, so why say twenty-six?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Without a child'? Then three days should also be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason she could last twenty-five days was the fourteen pure days that come from the child. If there is no child, nothing makes the bleeding pure. Then three bleeding זיבה days in a row already make her a זבה, so the number twenty-six makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: With three (days)
It is enough

phrases.english: Without a child?
Three days should also be enough!
phrases.notes: Without a child there are no pure labor-pain days, so three bleeding days in a row already make her a זבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּלֹא וָלָד? בִּתְלָתָא נָמֵי סַגִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the words 'without a child' in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'without a child' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no child, the purity of labor pains does not apply, so three days should make her a זבה, not twenty-six.

steps.title: רב ששת changes the wording to 'where there is a child'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says to read the ברייתא as 'where there is a child.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Say instead 'where there is a child.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is a real pregnancy, the twenty-six days make perfect sense, because the fourteen pure days apply. So רב ששת simply flips 'without a child' into 'with a child.'

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)

phrases.english: רב ששת said:
Say 'in a case where there is a child.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to talk about a woman with no child at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really talks about a woman who is carrying a child.

steps.title: רבא objects that the ברייתא clearly says 'without a child'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב ששת's change, because the ברייתא openly says 'without a child.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But it teaches 'without a child'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not want to turn the text into the opposite of what it says. The words 'without a child' are written plainly, so they must mean something.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (the text says)

phrases.english: רבא said to him:
But it teaches 'without a child'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא ״בְּלֹא וָלָד״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ששת's change to the wording
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against the plain words of the ברייתא, which say 'without a child.'

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא teaches two cases, a real child and a נפל
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא teaches twenty-six days for a real child, and only three days for a נפל, because labor pains do not make bleeding pure for a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what it means: It is impossible for her to have labor pains for twenty-six days where there is a child and not give birth as a זבה. And where there is no real child, only a נפל, with three days she also becomes a זבה. Why? There is no purity of labor pains for a נפל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer. He keeps the words 'without a child' and reads the ברייתא as two separate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a real child, the limit is twenty-six days, as the ברייתא said. 'Without a child' means the birth is only a נפל, a baby that cannot live. Labor pains with a נפל do not make the bleeding pure, so she becomes a זבה after only three days, like any other woman.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
A baby that is not able to live
The purity of labor pains does not apply to a נפל

steps.whatToRemember: With a real child, labor pains can keep her from being a זבה for up to twenty-five days, but at twenty-six she will be a זבה. With a נפל, labor pains do not help at all, so three days make her a זבה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'without a child' means she was never pregnant. רבא says it means the baby is a נפל.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said,
this is what it is saying:
It is impossible for her to have labor pains

phrases.aramaic: עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה יוֹם בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ וָלָד
phrases.english: for twenty-six days in a case where there is a child
and not be a woman who gives birth as a זבה,
and in a case where there is no child, only a נפל,
with three days she also becomes a זבה.
What is the reason?
There is no labor-pain purity for a נפל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's rejected answer with a new reading that keeps the words of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא as teaching two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Without a child' seemed to mean no pregnancy at all, which made the number twenty-six look wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Twenty-six days applies to a real child. 'Without a child' means a נפל, and then three days are enough because labor-pain purity does not apply to a נפל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a new rule: the purity of labor pains only applies to a baby that can live, not to a נפל.

steps.title: Labor bleeding within eighty days of a girl's birth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a woman in labor within 80 days of giving birth to a girl sees only pure blood until the child comes out. רבי אליעזר says it is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman in labor pains within eighty days of giving birth to a girl: all blood she sees is pure until the child comes out. רבי אליעזר says it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a ruling about a woman who goes into labor during the 80 days after giving birth to a girl. The חכמים and רבי אליעזר disagree about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a girl is born, the mother is impure for 14 days, and then blood she sees in the next 66 days is pure. Those 66 days are the 'days of purity' inside the 80. Here she goes into labor again during that time, and the question is whether that bleeding is still pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman having labor pains (hard labor) before giving birth
The 80 days after giving birth to a girl (14 impure days plus 66 days of pure blood)
The child (the baby being born)
Rules that it is impure

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman having labor pains within eighty days of giving birth to a female
all blood that she sees is pure
until the child comes out
And רבי אליעזר deems it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' הַמְקַשָּׁה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים שֶׁל נְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It builds on the earlier idea that labor pains can make blood pure from זיבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים say blood from labor during the 80 days after a girl's birth is pure until the child comes out. רבי אליעזר says it is impure.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי אליעזר with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue: the Torah was lenient about labor blood even in a strict setting. So in a setting where it is already lenient about calm blood, it should surely be lenient about labor blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי אליעזר: Where the Torah was strict about calm bleeding, it was still lenient about labor bleeding. Here it is lenient even about calm bleeding. Doesn't it make sense that we should be lenient about labor bleeding?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי אליעזר's view using a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, blood with no labor pains (דם השופי) is impure, yet blood with labor pains (דם הקושי) is treated leniently. During the days of purity, even calm blood is pure. So, they argue, labor blood should certainly be pure then too.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Calm blood: bleeding that comes without labor pains
Labor blood: bleeding that comes with labor pains

phrases.english: They said to רבי אליעזר:
And what if, in a place where the Torah was strict with calm blood,
phrases.notes: This means a regular time, outside the days of purity. There, bleeding with no labor pains is impure.

phrases.english: it was lenient with blood of labor pains;
then in a place where it was lenient with calm blood,
phrases.notes: This means the days of purity after a birth, when even ordinary bleeding is pure.

phrases.english: is it not logical that we should be lenient with blood of labor pains?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהֶחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that labor blood in the days of purity is impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if labor blood is treated leniently even where calm blood is impure, it must be pure where calm blood is already pure.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers with the rule of דיו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that a קל וחומר can't teach more than its source. The source only removed טומאת זיבה, so here too she is still impure as a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source. What was the Torah lenient about there? Only the impurity of זיבה. But she is still impure as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his view. He limits how far the חכמים' קל וחומר can go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון says a conclusion can't be stronger than the case it came from. Labor pains normally only keep her from becoming a זבה; she can still become a נדה. So even with the קל וחומר, labor blood in the days of purity makes her a נדה, and it is not fully pure.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: What is learned from a קל וחומר can only be as strong as its source, not stronger
The impurity of a זבה (bleeding outside the normal time)
The impurity of a woman in her regular menstrual state

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים say labor blood in the days of purity is fully pure. רבי אליעזר uses דיו to say labor pains only save her from זיבה, not from being a נדה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not reject the קל וחומר. He accepts it but limits it with דיו, so it only gives what the source gives: protection from זיבה, not from נדה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic use of the rule of דיו, a basic limit on every קל וחומר.

phrases.english: He said to them:
It is enough for what comes out of the reasoning
phrases.notes: The 'reasoning' here is the קל וחומר the חכמים just made.

phrases.english: to be like the case it is learned from.
From what was the Torah lenient with her?
From the impurity of זיבה,
but she is impure with the impurity of a נדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' קל וחומר from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenger's proof using the rule of דיו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר would make labor blood in the days of purity completely pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר only teaches what its source teaches: freedom from זיבה. She is still impure as a נדה.

steps.title: A ברייתא finds the חכמים' ruling in the word ״תֵּשֵׁב״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from the word ״תֵּשֵׁב״ that labor blood within 80 days of a girl's birth is pure. רבי אליעזר still disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: ״תֵּשֵׁב״ (she shall sit) comes to include a woman in labor within eighty days of a girl's birth, teaching that all blood she sees is pure until the child comes out. And רבי אליעזר says it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that gives a פסוק as the source for the חכמים' ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made the חכמים' view sound like it comes only from a קל וחומר. The ברייתא shows it is also learned from an extra word in the פסוק, ״תֵּשֵׁב״. רבי אליעזר's disagreement stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: 'She shall sit/observe', the word in the פסוק about the days of pure blood
To include: to add a case the פסוק does not openly mention
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
"She shall sit"

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת הַמְקַשָּׁה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים שֶׁל נְקֵבָה,
phrases.english: comes to include a woman in labor pains within eighty days of a female,
that all blood she sees is pure
until the child comes out,
and רבי אליעזר deems it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן תֵּשֵׁב לְרַבּוֹת הַמְקַשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the new משנה by giving a פסוק as the source for the חכמים' ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים' ruling that labor blood during the 80 days after a girl's birth is pure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא learning from the word ״תֵּשֵׁב״ (ויקרא 12:5)

steps.title: The Rabbis' first logical argument against רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue with a קל וחומר: the Torah was lenient about labor blood before birth, so it should surely be lenient about labor blood after birth, during the days of purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי אליעזר: Before a birth, the Torah is strict about calm bleeding, yet after a birth it is lenient about calm bleeding. Before a birth, the Torah is already lenient about labor bleeding. So surely after a birth we should be lenient about labor bleeding too.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, the חכמים challenge רבי אליעזר with a קל וחומר. They are trying to prove that labor blood during the days of purity is completely pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calm bleeding (no labor pains) before birth makes her a זבה, which is strict. After birth, the same calm bleeding is pure, which is lenient. Since labor bleeding is treated leniently even before birth, where things are strict, the חכמים say it should surely be lenient after birth, where things are already easy.

keyTerms.meaning: Calm, easy bleeding that comes without labor pains
Hard labor; bleeding that comes with labor pains
'Is it not logical?' This is the closing line of a קל וחומר
Was strict / was lenient

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of bleeding. שופי means calm bleeding with no pain, and קושי means bleeding that comes with labor pains. The whole argument depends on keeping them apart.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
And just as, in a place where [the Torah] was strict
with calm bleeding before the child is born,
phrases.notes: Calm bleeding before the birth makes her a זבה. That is the 'strict' part.

phrases.english: it was lenient with calm bleeding after the child is born;
then where it was lenient with labor bleeding before the child is born,
is it not logical that we should be lenient
with labor bleeding after the child is born?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהֶחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 17. It spells out the חכמים's argument against רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that labor blood within the days of purity is impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the Torah was lenient with labor blood even before birth, where it was strict, so it should surely be lenient after birth, where it is already lenient.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers: a logical argument can't go beyond its source
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers with דיו: the source only removed טומאת זיבה, so labor blood after birth still makes her a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What we learn from a logical argument can only be as strong as its source. What did the Torah let her off from? Only the impurity of זיבה. But the blood still makes her impure as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends himself against the חכמים's קל וחומר. He does not reject the argument. He limits how far it can go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before birth, labor blood only escapes זיבה impurity. It still counts as נדה impurity. Because of דיו, the conclusion can't be bigger than the source, so after birth too she escapes only זיבה and is still a נדה.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for what we learn from a קל וחומר to be like its source, and no more
The impurity of a זבה, from bleeding outside the normal time
The impurity of a woman in her monthly period

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of דיו is a general rule for every קל וחומר. Here it is the whole basis of רבי אליעזר's position.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין
phrases.english: He said to them: It is enough for what comes from the logical argument
to be like its source.
From what did [the Torah] let her off?
From the impurity of זיבה,
but it does make her impure with the impurity of a נדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the קל וחומר using the rule of דיו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר would make labor blood after birth completely pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר can only remove טומאת זיבה, just like its source. She is still impure as a נדה.

steps.title: The Rabbis try a second version of the argument
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים build the קל וחומר a different way, comparing labor blood to the calm blood of the same time period.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We will answer you a different way. Before a birth, the Torah is strict about calm bleeding, yet it is lenient about the labor bleeding of that same time. After a birth, the Torah is already lenient about calm bleeding. So surely we should be lenient about the labor bleeding of that time too.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים rebuild their קל וחומר with a new pairing. They hope this version avoids רבי אליעזר's answer of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version compared before-birth with after-birth. This version compares the two kinds of bleeding within each period. Before birth, labor blood is easier than calm blood. So after birth, when even calm blood is pure, labor blood should surely be pure as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A different version or wording of the argument
'That comes with it', meaning the labor bleeding of that same time period
Answering back; arguing in reply

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הֲרֵי אָנוּ מְשִׁיבִין לְךָ לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר,
phrases.english: They said to him: We will answer you with a different version:
And just as, in a place where it was strict
with calm bleeding before the child is born,
it was lenient with the labor bleeding that goes with it;
phrases.notes: 'With it' means the labor bleeding of that same time, before the birth.

phrases.english: then where it was lenient with calm bleeding after the child is born,
is it not logical that we should be lenient with the labor bleeding that goes with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הֲרֵי אָנוּ מְשִׁיבִין לְךָ לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 deflects the first קל וחומר, the חכמים offer a second version of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that labor blood within the days of purity is impure as נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inside each period, labor blood is treated more easily than calm blood. After birth even calm blood is pure, so labor blood should surely be pure.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר stands firm: דיו applies no matter how you argue
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says that however many versions they bring, the rule of דיו still limits the result. She is freed only from זיבה and is still a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Even if you argue back all day long, it is enough for what we learn from a logical argument to be like its source. What did the Torah let her off from? Only the impurity of זיבה. But the blood still makes her impure as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the second version with the same rule as before. This ends the debate in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the shape of the קל וחומר does not change its source. The source is still labor blood before birth, and that is only freed from זיבה impurity. So any קל וחומר built on it can only free her from זיבה, never from נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole day long; however much you keep arguing
Makes her impure

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים say labor blood within 80 days after a girl's birth is completely pure. רבי אליעזר says that because of דיו, it is only free of טומאת זיבה and still makes her a נדה.

phrases.english: He said to them: Even if you argue back
the whole day long,

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן,
phrases.english: it is enough for what comes from the logical argument to be like its source.
From what did [the Torah] let her off? From the impurity of זיבה,
but it does make her impure with the impurity of a נדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אֲפִילּוּ אַתֶּם מְשִׁיבִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20's second קל וחומר by repeating the rule of דיו from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the rule of דיו again, saying it holds for any version of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The new version of the קל וחומר might get around דיו and make labor blood fully pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: No version can go beyond the source, so she is freed only from זיבה and is still impure as a נדה.

steps.title: רבא: רבי אליעזר wins using the Rabbis' own reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי אליעזר beat the חכמים. They read ״דָּמָהּ״ as 'her own blood, not the child's,' so ״מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ״ must likewise mean only her own blood is purified, not labor blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: With this argument רבי אליעזר beat the Rabbis. Didn't you say that ״דָּמָהּ״ means blood that comes because of herself, and not because of the child? Then the same goes for ״וְטָהֲרָה מִמְּקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ״: it means only blood that comes because of herself, and not blood because of the child.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a strong argument for רבי אליעזר. It uses the very same reading the חכמים used for their own side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים learned from ״דָּמָהּ״ that labor blood before birth is not זיבה, because it comes from the child and not from the woman herself. רבא says: read ״דָּמֶיהָ״ in the purity פסוק the same way. Then the Torah's promise of purity after birth covers only her own blood, not labor blood. That is exactly רבי אליעזר's position.

keyTerms.meaning: He beat them, won the argument against them
Because of herself; her own natural bleeding
Because of the child; blood caused by labor
The source of her blood (ויקרא 12:7)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a classic גמרא move: you take the other side's own method of reading a פסוק and show it supports you.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With this, Rabbi Eliezer beat the Rabbis:
Didn't you say "her blood":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:25. The חכמים used this word to show that labor blood before birth isn't זיבה.

phrases.english: her blood that comes because of herself
and not because of the child?
So too: "and she shall be purified from the source of her blood":
her blood that comes because of herself is pure
and not blood that comes because of the child.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּהָא זַכִּינְהוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over the קל וחומר and דיו, רבא gives a reading of the פסוק that settles the debate in favor of רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that labor blood after birth is not covered by the purity of the days of purity
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים' own reading of ״דָּמָהּ״, applied in the same way to ״מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ״ (ויקרא 12:7)

steps.title: Why not split the rule between the נדה days and the זיבה days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view. Labor blood after birth should make her a נדה only during the נדה days, and leave her pure during the זיבה days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: if she sees labor blood during the days of נדה, she is a נדה, and if she sees it during the days of זיבה, she is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a challenge on רבי אליעזר's view. It suggests that labor blood should be treated differently depending on which days it falls in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said labor blood is freed from זיבה but still makes her a נדה. Ordinary blood seen during the זיבה days can only bring זיבה, not נדה. So during those days, labor blood that is freed from זיבה should leave her completely pure. Why should she be a נדה throughout the whole period?

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; it offers a different possibility
The seven days when a woman's bleeding makes her a נדה
The eleven days after the נדה days, when bleeding can make her a זבה

phrases.english: But say: during the days of niddah, she is a niddah,
and during the days of ziva, she is pure?
phrases.notes: Since labor blood can't bring זיבה, and the זיבה days can't bring נדה, nothing would be left to make her impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: בִּימֵי נִדָּה — נִדָּה, בִּימֵי זִיבָה — טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tests רבי אליעזר's conclusion by asking whether the rule should change depending on the days.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that labor blood after birth makes her a נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Labor blood is freed only from זיבה. During the זיבה days, blood can only bring זיבה, so labor blood there should leave her pure.

steps.title: 'She shall sit' means one rule for the whole period
steps.stepSummary: The word ״תֵּשֵׁב״ teaches that the whole period after birth is one 'sitting' with one rule. You cannot split it into נדה days and זיבה days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says ״תֵּשֵׁב״, 'she shall sit.' This means one sitting for all of the days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the word ״תֵּשֵׁב״. The whole purity period is treated as one single unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes the days after birth as one 'sitting.' So the same law must apply to labor blood throughout that time. Since in the first days it makes her a נדה, it makes her a נדה during the whole period.

keyTerms.meaning: She shall sit, or remain (ויקרא 12:5)
One sitting, a single unit of time with one rule

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, labor blood after birth is never זיבה, but it makes her a נדה the whole time. ״תֵּשֵׁב״ teaches that the period is one unit.

phrases.english: The verse says: "She shall sit":
one sitting for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״תֵּשֵׁב״ — יְשִׁיבָה אַחַת לְכוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a פסוק that makes the whole period one unit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule could change between the נדה days and the זיבה days.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״תֵּשֵׁב״ makes the whole period one sitting, so labor blood makes her a נדה throughout.

steps.title: New משנה: the eleven days are presumed pure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. During all eleven days of זיבה, a woman is presumed to be pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: During all eleven days, she is presumed to be pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new משנה. It gives a new rule about the eleven days of זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eleven days that follow the seven נדה days are given a חזקה of purity. We assume she is pure during that time unless we know otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The eleven days of זיבה that follow the seven נדה days
A presumption of purity

phrases.english: Mishnah:
All the eleven days
are in the presumption of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' כׇּל אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּחֶזְקַת טׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic, after the discussion of labor blood ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the eleven days of זיבה, a woman is presumed pure.
